title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X is a cylinder, i.e. a compact annulus S^1×[0,1] with no chosen orientation. The page continues the previous one, where the twist maps g_a(z,s) = (z·exp(2iπ a s), s) restrict to the identity on ∂X exactly when a ∈ Z.

Step 1: three ±1-torsors. Grothendieck attaches to X three 2-element sets, each a torsor under {±1}:
- ε0(X) = π0(∂X), the choice of one of the two boundary components;
- ε1(X), the choice of one of the two generators of π1(X) ≅ H1(X) ≅ Z;
- ω(X), the choice of one of the two orientations of X.

Step 2: the orientation is a product of the other two. He states a canonical isomorphism of {±1}-torsors ω(X) ≅ ε0(X) ∧ ε1(X), the contracted product. Concretely, choose a boundary component S (α ∈ ε0) and an orientation β of S. Since H1(S) ≅ H1(X), β is a generator, i.e. an element of ε1. The pair (α, β) determines the orientation of X whose boundary orientation on S is β. Changing either α or β flips the result, which is exactly what the contracted product expresses.

Step 3: the twist number of a boundary-fixing map. Let u be a homeomorphism of X that is the identity on ∂X (a power of the Dehn twist, e.g. g_a with a ∈ Z). Lift u to the universal cover X̃ ≅ R×[0,1].
- For a chosen boundary component S, there is a unique lift ũ^(S) that is the identity over S.
- Over the other component S' = ∂X \ S, this lift acts by a deck transformation τ_n, with n ∈ H1(S') ≅ H1(X).
- Exchanging the roles of S and S' gives ũ^(S') = τ_n^{-1} ũ^(S) = τ_{-n} ũ^(S), since deck transformations commute with lifts.
- So the integer n changes sign when the reference boundary component is changed.

Step 4: conclusion. The invariant n is canonically an element of H1(X) ∧_{±1} ε0(X), with no choices made. Writing H1(X) = Z ∧_{±1} ε1(X) and using Step 2:
H1(X) ∧ ε0(X) ≅ Z ∧_{±1} (ε1(X) ∧ ε0(X)) ≅ Z ∧_{±1} ω(X).
Therefore the group of isotopy classes of homeomorphisms of the annulus fixing the boundary is canonically Z twisted by the orientation torsor, Z(ω(X)). Once X is oriented, there is a canonical positive Dehn twist, independent of any orientation of the core curve or choice of boundary component.

What it serves. This is a basic building block for the Teichmüller tower, where twists around pinched curves generate the relevant inertia. It is the topological shadow of the fact that, for complex (hence canonically oriented) surfaces, the twist or inertia group is canonically Z(1) = 2πiZ; Grothendieck's Esquisse uses Ẑ(1) as the Galois-equivariant form of this.
errors: Slip in the manuscript: 'Soit un autom. de α' must mean an automorphism of X (α denotes a boundary component).
No mathematical error. The sign rule ũ^{S'} = τ_{-n} ũ^S is correct. The iso ω ≅ ε0∧ε1 depends on a boundary-orientation convention (e.g. outward normal first), which is implicit but harmless.

ideas.what: Orientation torsor of an annulus as contracted product of the boundary-component torsor and the generator-of-H1 torsor
ideas.modern_name: Torsor bookkeeping of orientations; boundary orientation convention

ideas.what: The twist number of a boundary-fixing homeomorphism of an annulus, defined via lifts to the universal cover, is canonically in H1(X)⊗ε0(X) ≅ Z(ω(X)); the mapping class group of the annulus rel boundary is canonically Z twisted by orientation
ideas.modern_name: Dehn twist / annulus twist number; left vs right Dehn twist depends only on orientation; Z(1)-twist of inertia
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dehn; folklore in mapping class group theory; Z(1)-inertia in the Galois/Teichmüller setting: Grothendieck (Esquisse), Ihara, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: The Z(1)/Ẑ(1) twisting of Dehn-twist inertia appears in spirit in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this precise annulus computation is not known to be published

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, choice-free derivation of a standard fact: the Dehn twist of an annulus is canonically an element of Z twisted by the orientation torsor, as a topological model of Z(1). It is useful bookkeeping for the Teichmüller tower but contains nothing absent from the literature.

'si on a une compos. du bord' → 'si on a une compos. S du bord (α ∈ ε0(X)) et une orientation du bord (β ∈ ε1(X) = un des deux génér. de H1(S))'
'on a une orientation de X : celle qui induit β sur α'
'par une élément' → 'par un élément n ∈ H1(S') ≃ H1(X)'
'Si on remplace S par S', on obtient ũ^(S') qui...' (the '[-change-]' is crossed out)
